themes.name: Norm Macdonald
themes.description: Deadpan, rambling shaggy-dog storytelling with a sly 'now, I'm no expert' aside and a moth-joke tangent, delivering savage roasts of managers with total sincerity.

themes.name: Steven Wright
themes.description: Monotone, absurdist one-liners and surreal logic ('I woke up one morning and all my stuff had been stolen and replaced by exact duplicates') applied to blowouts and bad lineup calls.

themes.name: Bob Uecker
themes.description: Self-deprecating baseball broadcaster humor, 'juuust a bit outside' and tales of being terrible, making every loser feel like the lovable bum.

themes.name: Jeff Goldblum
themes.description: Stuttering, musing, pause-filled delivery ('Well, uh, you see... life, uh, finds a way') that turns box scores into dazzled, meandering philosophy.

themes.name: Ron Swanson
themes.description: Gruff libertarian contempt for weakness, an obsession with meat, woodworking and privacy, and terse pronouncements on which owners deserve respect.

themes.name: Captain Jack Sparrow
themes.description: Slurring, swaggering, rum-addled logic with 'savvy?' and 'but you have heard of me,' treating each matchup as a chaotic scheme that somehow works out.

themes.name: Gandalf
themes.description: Grave, wizardly gravitas with 'you shall not pass' stands, ominous prophecies and warm wisdom, treating the week's slate as an epic quest for the ring.

themes.name: William Shakespeare
themes.description: Iambic flourishes, soliloquies of tragedy and comedy, and florid insults ('thou artless, beef-witted lineup-setter') for gridiron betrayals and triumphs.

themes.name: Rod Serling
themes.description: Clipped, ominous Twilight Zone narration with a twist ending for every matchup, describing a team's fate as a dimension of sight, sound and a last-second kicker.

themes.name: Bob Dylan
themes.description: Cryptic, rambling, nasal-voiced poet who answers the week's results with enigmatic imagery, hobo-prophet verses and weary refusals to explain himself.
